# Herdr

Herdr is a terminal workspace manager for AI coding agents: a background server owns real terminal processes (panes, tabs, workspaces), clients attach to render them, and panes survive detach. It is mouse-first and agent-aware.

## Use these resources only if your task asks for them

- Help a human understand or set up Herdr for the first time:
  https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/agent-guide.md
- Debug or investigate a problem with Herdr:
  https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/docs/troubleshooting/
- Control Herdr panes, agents, or workspaces programmatically:
  Run `herdr --skill` (if a Herdr skill is not already in your context) or read
  https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/docs/socket-api/

## Canonical documentation

- Docs: https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/docs/
- CLI reference: https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/docs/cli-reference/
- Configuration: https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/docs/configuration/
- Socket API: https://herdr.chefgroep.nl/docs/socket-api/

## Detecting the runtime

- `HERDR_ENV=1` is set inside a Herdr pane.
- The `herdr` CLI talks to the running server over a local socket. Clear
  `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` / `HERDR_CLIENT_SOCKET_PATH` when driving a fresh build.

## Key facts for agents

- Panes keep running when the client detaches or the terminal closes.
- Agent state (`working`, `blocked`, `done`, `idle`, `unknown`) is detected
  from process and terminal evidence, not reported by the pane app.
- Prefer `herdr pane ...` / `herdr workspace ...` / `herdr agent ...` over
  guessing public ids; use `herdr workspace list` / `herdr pane list` first.
